messages:
Marco Chen: Heads-up — customer reported apparent double provisional token charge when a streaming toolcall retried mid-response. Stack: streaming -> toolcall -> model-swap fallback -> reconnect.
Priya Narayan: hmm. any logs/trace ids?
Marco Chen: trace=tr_8f3a, attached snippet from router: `Reroute: session=ss_42 -> region-b fallback, model changed from rdx-2 to rdx-2-quant`. Client reconnected before final ACK.
Alex Gomez: classic provisional vs confirmed lifecycle. We mark provisional on stream start, confirm at session close. But reconnect+model-swap created two provisional ledgers and the reconciler merged incorrectly.
Jen Kim: Can we reproduce with a controlled script? I can run a canary that forces region fallback and immediate reconnect.
Marco Chen: repro script attached (ran on canary env). Important bits: client sends `stream_start`, server streams tokens, then mid-stream route fails -> `reroute_fallback`, new route resumes with `resume_prefix` that overlaps.
Priya Narayan: looks like resume_prefix copying causes the resumed stream to re-emit same prefix tokens which get counted again as provisional. We then later dedupe on confirmation, but UI shows the provisional spike and customers see a charge blip in the console.
Alex Gomez: two issues: 1) accounting model needs a canonical session id that survives route changes, 2) console should display provisional vs confirmed credits more clearly and not alarm on transient spikes.
Marco Chen: Agree. Currently router assigns ephemeral `session_shard` ids; proposal: embed `session_stable_id` propagated in handoff metadata. If present, ledger merges provisional entries by stable id.
Jen Kim: Implementation question: do we change internal API shape (`/start` payload) or piggyback on existing `handoff.metadata`?
Priya Narayan: piggybacking is faster but fragile. If we add `session_stable_id` to the start handshake we can guarantee plumbing through all proxies. Minimal proto change: `StartRequest { string stable_session_id = 6; }`.
Alex Gomez: telemetry: emit an event `session.stable_id.propagated` and `accounting.provisional_written(session_stable_id)` so we can query spikes by stable id. That will help postmortems.
billing-bot: Provisional charge created: id=pc_98765 amount=0.12 tokens=340 session=ss_42
Marco Chen: UX: Console should suppress provisional blips under X seconds or show them as gray until confirmed. Prefer add a small tooltip: "Provisional charges may be reconciled within 2 minutes."
Jen Kim: Ops impact — rollout plan? We need router + ledger + console changes. Can we do ledger dedupe-only fallback first?
Priya Narayan: Yes, ledger-side dedupe by `(stable_id, token_range_start)` is a safe intermediate. But without stable_id we fall back to heuristics: `trace_id + prefix_hash` which is flaky.
Alex Gomez: For short-term, add a reconciler job that post-processes recent provisional spikes and tags them with suspected duplicates, then the console can gray them out. Medium-term: handshake change + router propagation + metrics.
Marco Chen: Agreed. Action items: 1) Jen to run canary script + produce exact repro steps (ETA today). 2) Priya to prototype `session_stable_id` proto and backwards compat plan (ETA Tue). 3) Alex to add telemetry event proposals and sample Grafana queries (ETA Wed). 4) Ops will add temporary console note about provisional charges.
Jen Kim: I'll post the canary logs in #eng-sre after I run. Also adding a quick integration test to catch double provisional on resume.
Marco Chen: Thanks. One more edge case — toolcalls that truncate earlier tokens on the server side (due to tool-host timeout) then resume; make sure dedupe keys include toolcall id.
Priya Narayan: noted — include `toolcall_id` in ledger keys.
Alex Gomez: cc @billing-bot for any alerts we should suppress during the remediation rollout.
billing-bot: Alert suppressed for trace tr_8f3a per request by Marco Chen
ops-bot: Canary run scheduled by Jen Kim at 1719997850
Marco Chen: OK closing loop — we'll reconvene after canary. :thumbsup:
